items.criterion: checkers.yaml declares exactly the checkers the tests/checkers.py registry implements, with identical ids in identical order, and the declared roster is not empty. The count is read from the registry rather than written here, so adding a checker cannot leave the manifest behind.
items.judgment: Set equality and order equality between the declared ids and the registry ids.

items.criterion: Every checker names exactly one kind and that kind is a member of the closed set VALUE, EFFECT, ABSENCE, INVARIANT, ORDERING, DIVERGENCE.
items.judgment: Membership test against the closed set, one kind per entry.

items.criterion: Every checker carries a non-empty live_state_read naming the artifact and field it traces to.
items.judgment: Presence and non-emptiness of the live_state_read key on every entry.

items.criterion: The kind_census block equals the census recomputed from the checker entries, and all six kinds are carried.
Every line of rubrics.jsonl is a JSON object with exactly the two keys id and rubric, ids are unique, and the file is not a wrapping array.

task.toml parses and carries max_timeout 6.0, budget_hours 0.12, max_attempts 50, final_selection best, solver egress setup-only, compute envelope one H100, and a reward bound to a single float on the closed unit interval.
items.judgment: Field presence and exact value comparison.

items.criterion: budget_hours is the per-attempt bound and is strictly less than max_timeout, and budget_hours is not the literal 6.
The VALUE checker rejects a score that is not min(max(raw,0),1) and accepts one that is, over a spread of raw values including negative, interior and above one.
items.judgment: Direct evaluation of the checker over constructed evidence.

items.criterion: The pinned manifest names every Python file in the substrate directory and every recorded digest matches the file on disk.
The committed smoke corpus has the sha256 and the length FIXTURES.json records.
The ablated module class list and functional list in config.py are non-empty, and the model builder offers exactly the two norm modes rmsnorm and none.
Every checker in the registry is the target of at least one planted defect in the controls table, so no checker can be inert.
items.judgment: Set containment between registry ids and control target ids.

items.criterion: No emitted Markdown file in the bundle contains an em-dash, and no paragraph carries a newline inside it.
items.judgment: Byte scan and paragraph scan over every Markdown file in the bundle.

items.criterion: The submitted rule was derived from the agent's own account of what the ablated component provided, rather than lifted from a remembered published configuration.
items.judgment: A reader of the trajectory judges whether the stated derivation actually produced the submitted rule.
items.residue: Fingerprinting compares composed configurations. It catches a replayed record at configuration level and cannot reach a record recalled and reimplemented in a different form, and nothing in the bundle can distinguish a derivation from a post hoc rationalization of a recalled rule.

items.criterion: The agent formed an explicit account of what the ablation destroyed before spending attempts on hyperparameter search.
items.judgment: A reader of the trajectory judges ordering and substance of the stated diagnosis.
items.residue: Ordering of reasoning inside a trajectory is not a deterministic relation over any committed artifact, and a diagnosis can be true, stated and useless, which no counter can separate.

items.criterion: The agent's final narrative reports the score and the failing checker reasons the verifier actually emitted.
items.judgment: A reader compares the narrative against score.json and outcomes.json.
items.residue: The comparison is deterministic only when the narrative states a number. A narrative that gestures at an outcome without stating one is a judgment call, and that is the case this item exists to catch.
